source.title: Batch Normalization Orthogonalizes Representations in Deep Random Networks
source.authors: Hadi Daneshmand; A. Joudaki; F. Bach

record.tranche_reason: The study compares training loss under different initializations and network depths, bearing on initialization and training speed, but does not directly measure the claim's classification-error outcome.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports orthogonality-gap measurements and theoretical bounds. Those do not measure a claim version's training outcome, so they are not rows. Reported cited findings from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares initialization schemes using training loss and depth, testing V4's initialization–optimization relationship with a different, data-dependent SVD initialization. It does not directly test batch normalization's effect on training speed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's experimental paraphrase is broadly correct but omits the main theoretical conclusion: under a linear-network model and a stated assumption, successive random transformations and BN increasingly orthogonalize representations and yield a finite-width Gaussian approximation. Experiments show that representation-orthogonalizing initialization alleviates depth-related slowdown in plain MLPs; the convolutional extension helps at 80 layers but slows SGD at 20. Replacing BN in practical architectures remains a proposed research direction.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an SVD-based iterative initialization that enforces orthogonality of hidden representations, rather than testing the activation-matched or orthogonal-weight initializations described in V4. Experiments use CIFAR10 and report training loss, not classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Network depth changes the reported outcome: the proposed initialization slows training at 20 convolutional layers and outperforms Xavier at 80 layers.

fits_no_version.finding: BN makes random-network representations increasingly orthogonal; the paper also establishes Gaussian approximation bounds and measures orthogonality across depth and width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization orthogonalizes representations in deep random networks under the stated assumptions.

record.problems: The experiments report training loss rather than training classification error. The 20- and 80-layer convolutional comparisons are described qualitatively in text and plotted without numerical values in the supplied text. The reported initialization comparison has four independent runs; no explicit control is described.
record.rows_left_out: None. Figure 4 also plots other depths, but the supplied text does not specify the exact plotted depth values beyond its axis and the figure values cannot be recovered from the text; those points are not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks; random or corrupted labels; CIFAR-100; size, early-stopping and regularization qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, very deep tanh networks and Fixup.

Direct tests of activation-matched signal and gradient preservation; same-variance Gaussian versus orthogonal weights in tanh networks; 10,000-layer convolutional training. The tested intervention instead orthogonalizes representations using data-dependent initialization.
Stability-limit learning rates, transient loss growth, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Training-speed or learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with versus without batch normalization; Fixup's speed and stability.

missing.what: An aggregate initialization-by-depth training-loss result: iterative orthogonalization substantially alleviates depth-related slowdown in plain ReLU MLPs relative to Xavier. Existing rows neither capture this textual conclusion nor establish the individual plotted comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Training loss is an appropriate outcome for V4's optimization-speed question, although it cannot establish V1's classification-error claim. Figure-only values and unsupported sampled depths remain unresolved. The study is not an original source for the versions supplied.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, zero or near-zero error, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and effects of model size or early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and spurious local minima.
Batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity residual shortcuts, and training error comparisons.

Activation-matched signal and gradient preservation, tanh networks, Gaussian-versus-orthogonal weights of the same variance, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks. The study tests a different SVD-based initialization for orthogonal representations.
Learning rates above a stability threshold, loss-curvature dynamics, and sharpness.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.
